intent: Bring meta/scripts/disk_cleanup_check.sh (329 lines) under the 250-line cap by moving its formatting, sizing, confirmation and output helpers into a sourced lib.
scope: Non-goal: no change to which directories are checked, what is reported, or what --clean deletes
changes: Move the six colour constants and human_readable/dir_size_kb/report/confirm/try_clean into lib/disk_cleanup_common.sh.
Move the report-only loop and the summary block into print_report_only and print_summary in the same lib; the entry script now ends with two calls.

Add SCRIPT_DIR resolved from BASH_SOURCE so the source line works from any cwd, and set CLEAN/TOTAL_RECLAIMABLE before sourcing, since confirm reads CLEAN and report accumulates into TOTAL_RECLAIMABLE.

verification.command: meta/scripts/trace_shell_split.sh <script> --stub du --out before.txt (detached worktree at the pre-split commit), then again after the split, then diff
verification.evidence: TRACE IDENTICAL -- exit status, the ordered list of stubbed `du -sk` calls, stdout and stderr all byte-identical. This is the check that matters here: the seam passes state (report mutates TOTAL_RECLAIMABLE, confirm reads CLEAN), so a static check could not have caught a break.

verification.command: bash ~/testsAndMisc/meta/scripts/disk_cleanup_check.sh (run for real from /tmp, not from the script's own directory)
verification.evidence: exit 0, full report against real data: 303.7 GB auto-reclaimable, current usage 1445.6 GB / 3665.4 GB (42%). Running from a different cwd confirms SCRIPT_DIR resolves the lib correctly -- a known failure mode for split scripts. Dry-run default, nothing deleted.

verification.command: bash -n + shellcheck -x on the entry, shellcheck on the lib, shfmt -d on both
verification.evidence: All exit 0 with no output. An initial SC2034 (RED appears unused) was resolved by moving print_report_only -- which uses RED -- into the lib, rather than by adding a suppression.

risks: The lib depends on CLEAN and TOTAL_RECLAIMABLE being set by the caller before it is sourced. That is documented in its header comment; sourcing it standalone would leave confirm reading an unset CLEAN.

`bc` was briefly stubbed during the first baseline attempt, which produced 'printf: invalid number' noise -- bc is a calculator, not a mutator. The recorded baseline uses real bc and has empty stderr.
rollback: git revert the commit; the helpers return inline and lib/disk_cleanup_common.sh disappears.
Re-run the script from any directory and confirm it prints the analysis table and a non-zero total.
